body.statement: Let \(\mathcal P\) be an input-free COPAG and let \(A_0,B_0\subseteq V\) be disjoint with \(A_0\neq\varnothing\).  If \(\operatorname{sIDP}(\mathcal P;A_0,B_0,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) returns \(\operatorname{Fail}\), then \(P_{\mathbf M}(A_0\mid\operatorname{do}(B_0),S=\mathbf 1)\) is not identified over \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).

source.locator: Theorem 4.15, sIDP completeness for input-free COPAGs
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 4.15 (Main result V: sIDP and causal calculus are complete). Let P=(empty,V,E) be a COPAG and A,B subsets of V be disjoint with A nonempty. If sIDP(P;A,B) outputs Fail, then P_M(X_A | X_S=1 || do(X_B)) is not identifiable in M_d^+(P).
